# id: # Pinned GGUF candidates for the llama-server latency sweep (benchmark_llm_serve.sh).
# Byte counts and SHA-256 values are the Hugging Face LFS object ids; revisions
# are the repository commits pinned at the same time.
# An id containing "-mtp-" tells benchmark_llm_serve.sh to run that model twice,
# once plain and once with --spec-type draft-mtp (depth from --mtp-n-max).
# ROUND 2, informed by the 2026-08-13 sweep on the 8 GB CM5. Measured there:
#   arm                          TTFT later   decode    vs base   peak RSS
#   Qwen3-1.7B Q4_0 (baseline)      0.82 s    9.74 t/s    100%     2336 MiB
#   Qwen3.5-2B Q4_0 plain           1.20 s    6.85 t/s     70%     2632 MiB
#   Qwen3.5-2B Q4_0 MTP n-max 6     1.16 s    3.36 t/s     35%     2914 MiB
#   LFM2-8B-A1B Q4_0                0.85 s   11.05 t/s    113%     7291 MiB  (swapped)
#   Granite-4.0-H-Tiny Q4_0         0.92 s    7.67 t/s     79%     7567 MiB  (swapped)
# Conclusions carried into this manifest:
#   - LFM2 is the only candidate that BEAT the baseline, and it did so on decode
#     (11.05 vs 9.74) while matching later-turn TTFT. It is the one worth saving.
#     Its only problem is footprint, so round 2 re-tests it small enough to fit.
#   - Granite is dropped: slower than baseline AND the largest footprint of all,
#     because its hybrid-Mamba SSM state cost 3788 MiB on top of 3779 MiB of
#     weights. Nothing about it is worth another 25 minutes.
#   - Qwen3.5-2B stays only as the denominator for the MTP retry.
# Sizing rule used below. Measured overhead above weights was ~2.8 GiB for LFM2.
# A production-viable model must leave room for resident Moonshine (~614 MiB)
# plus the daemon and OS (~500 MiB) inside ~7900 MiB, so peak RSS must stay under
# roughly 6500 MiB — meaning weights under about 3700 MiB.
# 3506 MiB. Unsloth's dynamic quant keeps attention and embedding tensors at
# higher precision than a uniform Q3, so it is the best quality available at a
# size that actually fits. This is the headline candidate for round 2.
lfm2-8b-a1b-ud-q3-k-xl
# 3812 MiB. Just over the sizing rule — included deliberately to find where the
# cliff actually is rather than trusting the arithmetic. If this one fits, the
# UD-Q3_K_XL row is the safe choice and this is the quality-preferred one.
lfm2-8b-a1b-q3-k-m
